holidays.name: National Dog Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate dogs of every breed, size, and level of couch-hogging. Owners shower pups with treats, extra walks, and social media tributes, while shelters push adoption of dogs in need.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2004 by pet and family lifestyle expert Colleen Paige, who also created National Cat Day and National Puppy Day. She chose August 26 because it was the day her family adopted a sheltie when she was ten.
holidays.funFact: Colleen Paige picked the date because of her childhood sheltie, and the holiday now encourages the rescue of an estimated 10,000 dogs each year.

holidays.name: National Cherry Popsicle Day
holidays.description: A frosty salute to the classic red frozen treat that stains your lips and fingers. Perfect for the tail end of summer, when you need one more reason to be sticky.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday that emerged from the popularity of fruit-flavored ice pops. The popsicle itself was reportedly invented by accident in 1905 by 11-year-old Frank Epperson, who left a soda mixture with a stirring stick outside overnight.
holidays.funFact: Frank Epperson first called his invention the 'Epsicle' before his own kids convinced him to rename it 'Popsicle,' after 'Pop.'

holidays.name: Women's Equality Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the certification of the 19th Amendment, which granted American women the right to vote. It is marked with parades, speeches, voter registration drives, and celebrations of progress toward equality.
holidays.origin: Certification of the 19th Amendment took place on August 26, 1920. Congress designated the day in 1971 at the urging of Representative Bella Abzug, and presidents have issued proclamations for it ever since.
holidays.funFact: The amendment's ratification came down to a single vote in Tennessee, cast by 24-year-old legislator Harry T. Burn, who switched his vote after getting a letter from his mother telling him to 'be a good boy' and support it.

holidays.name: National Cheese Pizza Day (Unofficial Pizza-Adjacent Fun)
holidays.description: Also known as a day to enjoy the purest pizza form, with no toppings, no fuss, and no arguments about pineapple. Just cheese, sauce, and crust, as nature intended.
holidays.origin: A social media-driven food observance within the crowded calendar of pizza holidays, celebrating the simplicity of the plain cheese pie, which many pizzerias consider the true test of their craft.
holidays.funFact: Many pizza experts say the simple Margherita, named after Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889, is the ancestor of the modern cheese pizza.

holidays.name: National Tug of War Day (Unofficial)
holidays.description: A day to grab a rope and test your strength, teamwork, and willingness to get dragged through mud. Perfect for picnics, family reunions, and settling disputes with dignity.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted observance inspired by the old sport of tug of war, which dates back thousands of years in cultures around the world.
holidays.funFact: Tug of war was an official Olympic event from 1900 to 1920, with teams from several countries competing for medals.
